messages:
Asha: putting a draft out for review — SI brokerage & split rules. Goal: cut down on ping-pong when multiple SIs claim the same account. High-level proposal below. Please react with :eyes: if you'll review.

Tom: quick q — are we defining % splits or owner assignment?

Asha: primary flow = owner assignment by claim window (48h). First-claim wins unless there's an active field engagement flagged in SFDC. If contested, Partnerships triage + sales leader decision within 24h. Splits only for co-sell situations > $100k ACV or when both SIs bring clearly scoped work.

Diego: 48h feels tight for enterprise where SI needs internal approvals. Can we do 72h for named accounts? Also we need a clear account-mapping precedence: dedicated territory owner > named AE > field-engaged SI.

Asha: good call — updated: 48h standard, 72h for named enterprise (ACV >= 200k) or when SI marks 'field-engaged'. We'll codify precedence order too.

Nina: legal note: watch out for partner MSAs and statements of work that create conflicting obligations. Add "no contract execution without legal sign-off" for contested-claims and any deal with split revenue.

Eve: ops note — marketplace will add claim metadata and a "provisional-claim" state. Example config payload we'll use for automation: 
```json
{
  "claim_window_hours": 48,
  "enterprise_claim_window_hours": 72,
  "escalation_owner": "partnerships@redwood.com",
  "co_sell_threshold_acv": 100000
}
```

marketplace-bot: automation created: webhook /partners/claims will emit events: claim.created, claim.contested, claim.resolved. Docs: https://internal.redwood.ai/partners/claims (staging).

Tom: for splits I propose default 70/30 in favor of the primary SI, unless both bring equivalent scope then 50/50. Prefer template to speed approvals.

Diego: i'd avoid hard-coded percentages. use default template 70/30 but allow Sales Ops + Partnerships to approve overrides per-deal.

Asha: agreed — default 70/30, overrides require Sales Ops + Partnerships sign-off recorded in SFDC under Partner Engagement. We'll include a short approval checklist.

Nina: also add a compliance/data-locality check when SI requires on-prem demos or customer data access. That should gate approvals.

Eve: I'll add extra fields to the claim webhook: "requires_on_prem_demo": true/false, "sensitive_data": true/false, and a link to the SFDC note.

Asha: next steps: Eve to add claim states + hooks; Nina to draft legal language; Diego to produce mapping rules (territory precedence list); Tom to confirm sales leader approval path. I will collect all inputs and circulate a short playbook by EOD Friday. If no blockers, react with :thumbsup:.

Tom: :thumbsup:

Diego: will do. :+1:

Nina: sending draft legal language today.

Eve: provisioning the webhook now — ping me for test events.

marketplace-bot: test event claim.created sent to staging at 1717706000
